title: News Tonight
subtitle: This program has no need for boring themes—hand the camera to the fangs and flying bullets!

items.text: News Tonight
Woods Near the Studio
She swiftly sidesteps, maintaining her balance as the bullet whizzes past her.
No second shot follows. The attacker is merely probing, not aiming to kill.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Who are you?!
The figure raises up a menacing dagger. The blade is slim, with a curved edge tapering to a point. A favorite of the Italian mafia.
More disturbing still is the scent, identical to the blood from Nora Ostern's house.
Focusing on the blade's trajectory, she bends her knees and leaps back. Feeling the tingle of blood rushing to her toes.
The assailant's attacks are random and almost playful.
Growing impatient, she knows she must end this fight quickly.
Seeing her chance, she lunges forward and grabs her attacker's neck, causing him to freeze. She has him now, and bares her fangs for the strike.
Suddenly, there is a sharpness at her throat. A glance confirms it, another blade.
In a fluid motion, she strikes at his wrist, forcing the knife from his hand as she pulls back from him.
The knife spins through the air and lands with a clink.
A beam of moonlight cuts through the trees, illuminating the path between them. In the half-light, Semmelweis recognizes his face.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You're ... with the Foundation ...

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Oh, it's you.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: I've heard about you, our "Red-Eyed Lazarus," who was half-dead one day and up and about the next.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: How did you find me?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I was in shadow form. How was I exposed? The scent from the recovery center? Or the shampoo I used yesterday?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Wolves can sniff out trouble from a mile away.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Of course, not all trouble is bad, if it's the right kind. Juicy gossip is the perfect appetizer for the diners around the Wiener Staatsoper!

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: All the young artists dreaming of making it big, building themselves up and tearing their so-called friends down.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: The over-loud whispers of some washed-up star about who is sleeping with who, declaring the truth of each and every kind of scandal.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: But you? You don't strike me as someone who dishes out catty remarks. No, you seem more like the type to cause all the wrong kind of trouble, like being picky, skipping bills, and laying ambushes.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Ambush? Was it not you that tried to kill me? Is this how you greet your colleagues?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: I haven't tried to kill you just yet, first I need you to tell me where Nora Ostern is.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Che cazzo! Why does everyone here love to vanish?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: What is it that you want from her? And under whose authority? No one mentioned any other agents being assigned to this mission.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Ah, so you're on a mission, huh, well, your business is none of my concern.
Pavia chuckles softly, wiping his blade with his shirt sleeve.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Allow me to ask again, why has the Timekeeper sent you to Vienna?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: I know nothing of the "why" at all, it isn't my job to ask. All I know is this Nora Ostern has something she wants, and I thought it best to have some fun in Vienna while I'm free.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Could it be that the Timekeeper ordered an egg from Nora Ostern? Are you here to pick it up for her?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Unbelievable! How could the Timekeeper have allowed this?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Well, my resignation letter is still sitting in her drawer, and it's been there for a while. So, I figured I might as well stay on the job for now.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Naturally, that doesn't mean I want any part in your little mission here.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But then you've already been to Nora Ostern's house. Were you the one that picked the lock on her drawer?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Hey, listen! I don't do that kind of delicate namby-pamby work. It wasn't me. Capiche?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: But I was there, and I didn't find what the boss was after. So, I waited around to see if someone else would have an explanation. Then some other woman came in smelling like burnt ... burnt something, anyways—

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: A woman was it; did you happen to catch a glimpse of her face?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Nah, she was just like you, hiding herself in the darkest shadows. What did you call that "Shadow Form"? Whatever. Don't tell me, I don't care what you call it.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: So, she's a vampire too.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Yeah, and a rude one at that. She didn't even bother with a greeting before charging at me. So, I, well, let's just say I aimed to slit her throat.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You fought?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: My first swipe missed—she was fast like you too. But she showed a weakness, and my second strike hit square on her shoulder.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Of course, then she went and grabbed some useless black egg and smashed it on me. Didn't hurt none, so I have to wonder what was she even thinking?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Ah, it's coming together clearly now. That explains the bloodstains. You wounded her, and she fled into this forest.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: You two have the same scent. So, when you went sneaking back in there like a ghost, I thought she must have come back for round two—though that would've been a pathetic fight.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Come to think of it, she had burns similar to yours as well.
Semmelweis chuckles as Pavia points to her neck. She has given up trying to mask her annoyance.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: What are the odds she'll survive your attack?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Survive? Not going to happen! She's like you, got those same eyes, and I know what that means.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: She won't last long. Not without fresh blood.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Perhaps, but if she is still bleeding, it means she has not run dry yet.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She will need blood to heal. And since she apparently hasn't succeeded in finding what she was looking for, she'll likely show up here again. We can use that to catch her.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: We? What's this "we" business? Leave me out of it.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Are we not colleagues?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: I wouldn't have taken you for the "teamwork" kind.
She shrugs as if reaffirming her noncommittal nature.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Forget it for now. You mentioned we have the same scent. That means she's also been exposed to mycelium. If so, she may very well be our kidnapper.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Oh yeah, and why would she be kidnapping those women? Do egg painters got tastier blood or something?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You're right. If all she wanted was their blood, wouldn't killing them outright be simpler?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Then it's money. It's got to be.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Money is certainly the most obvious motive, but the authorities haven't received any ransom demands.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Well, it's been so long since anyone has heard from them, maybe it was not a kidnapping but a killing, and they're just lying in a ditch somewhere rotting.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: No. The eggs still showed up in time for the festival. As curious as that is, for whatever reason they must still be out there.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: It seems this vampire kidnapped the artists to force them to make mycelium eggs, then spread them throughout the city.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Therefore, they must be held captive in some secret location, and if so, then her activities must keep close to that location. So that she can keep them monitored.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But if she's encountered you, she must fear being hunted. She won't risk returning there tonight.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: In that case, continuing to track her will only play into her hands. The longer we wait, the more danger her hostages are in.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Damn it. We need to figure out her identity quick, it will allow us to narrow down our investigation.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Hah! All that talk and you wind up back at clueless. Alright, you've roped me in, but my instinct still says: money.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Money is the greatest of all motives, delusion and desire mixed together. People always think just a little more money is all they need to change everything.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: You sound like one of those old drunks outside the theater, convinced they've found the winning lottery numbers on an old street sign!
She ignores Pavia's mocking, falling into deep contemplation.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: So then, why does she want these eggs? Or rather, why does she need the artists to make them for her? Is she not capable of doing so herself?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Could be any reason, who knows? All I can see is that she's using others for her own gain.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She targeted key members of the Artists' Guild, and did so by breaking into their homes to kidnap them. Evidently, she had intimate knowledge of the victims' personal lives.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: There were no signs of struggle at the scene, no forced entry marks on the doors, which suggests they knew each other. Perhaps the victims even let her in themselves.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: We can deduce that she knew the victims, logically she may have worked with them.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Yeah right, I'm sure these humans were just fine with inviting a blood-sucking vampire into their homes. What do you think, she just knocked on the door and asked for a bite?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Perhaps not, but it's possible she concealed her true nature. If she was a fellow artist, she could have used a work-related excuse to get inside.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: And since the eggs were placed around the city, she is using them for something grander than just their most obvious effects.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She's even seen to it that the festival proceeds without interruption, so that everyone will open their eggs together.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: If that's the case, then everyone along the parade route would be affected by the mycelium powder. That's her plan—she intends to dose the entire population of Vienna.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Then she must be observing everything. She will need to, to ensure it all goes to plan.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Wacko, taking control of an entire festival? So, what, does she intend to drink the whole of Vienna dry? Or carve it up into her own personal vampire fiefdom?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: I think she's just trying to goad you. Force you into searching for her everywhere. It's clever, I admit.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: She'll wait until the time is pitch perfect. Then she'll emerge and make her move. For her, evading capture now is simply a game.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: If you want to catch her, you'll have to play her game.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Play her game ...
There is something stirring in her mind.
An unmistakable sound pierces the air, breaking her from her thoughts—the wail of police sirens.

items.speaker: Police
items.text: Police! Hands up!
A bright white light pierces through the gaps between the trees. Instinctively, she raises her hands to shield her eyes from their lights.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Why are the police here?

items.speaker: Police
items.text: We were called over a break-in nearby, apparently, we're looking for a man and a woman. That sound like anyone you know?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Break-in? You mean at Nora Ostern's house. Officer, you will find I have an investigation permit from the Foundation. Oh! It's you!

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Hahaha! What, you really thought the regular old police were going to be on our tails that fast. Fat chance any of them are investigating that house tonight. They were just passing by.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Come on, have a little humor, sunshine.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: No, no. You bring up an excellent point, let's go to the station and make a report!
Semmelweis moves to grab Pavia's wrist, but he slips away like a snake.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Oh, now you're really surprising me.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Tell me, did the Foundation really fix you?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: That wild look in your eyes, is the beast inside finally tamed?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: After I was "freed," I couldn't help myself imagining those poor souls clinging and pleading for their lives under my knife.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Ah that fear, that delicious physical and mental reaction. Such thrilling memories.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: You're no different, blood-sucker. So, why don't we handle this in the most pleasurable way possible?
Pavia gestures.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Bam! A bullet right through the skull! Just like that. And you'd be cheering beside me, "Well done! You son-of-a-b***h! On to the next one!"

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: We've all got to get our kicks somewhere.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'm struggling to see your point.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: I mean that you can't exactly tell the cops I'm just your everyday casual door-crashing "gentleman thief," now, can you?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: They won't be inclined to work with you just because of that Foundation badge, more than likely they'll just brush you off.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: That's if they even listen, more than likely they'll just put me in a cage, and thank you for reporting this "suspicious activity." They won't give a toss.

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: And hell, let's imagine it does work out for you, eh, what then?

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: If the media catches wind, they'll blow things out of proportion and convince the public there's some bloodthirsty creature stalking the streets of Vienna. Panic everywhere, mass hysteria, think that will look good on your report?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: And what will they report about you "Dangerous former mercenary causes havoc in the streets?"

items.speaker: Pavia
items.text: Please, I don't give a damn about the media. But your bosses do.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I can respect that.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Then for tonight, we lie low. I can't have our actions at this pivotal time be excessively scrutinized.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Goodbye.
TO BE CONTINUED…
